subject: Finlytics — pricing guardrails, token economics & overage options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Finlytics call recap — token volumes, target $/1M, and overage approach

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the discovery: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use: real-time enrichment for dashboard queries + nightly batch embeddings for similarity search.
- Expected concurrency: spike to ~350 rps for short text generation during market opens; steady-state 25–40 rps otherwise.
- Token mix: ~70% generation (avg 60 tokens per request), 30% embeddings (avg 1 request per user/day).

Open asks we promised to follow up on:
1) A realistic monthly token window you want us to price against (min/expected/max). You mentioned a pilot in Dec — could you confirm expected pilot size?
2) Budget range target in $/month or target unit economics (you referenced target ~$900–1,100 per 1M tokens on the call — wanted to confirm).
3) Rate-limit tolerance and acceptable behavior during spikes: do you want burst tolerance, soft throttling, or guaranteed throughput?

What we propose (next steps / options):
- Pilot pricing tier (30-day, up to 150M tokens): flat unit price with one-time onboarding credits.
- Production recommendation: standard hosted with soft quota + burst buffer (short bursts up to 2.5x baseline for 10s windows) plus an optional reserved capacity route if you need strict SLAs.
- Overage options: 1) auto-pay overage at a slightly higher unit rate, 2) pre-purchased burst credits pack (discounted), or 3) soft cap with notification and manual approval for increases.

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf (sample unit tiers) and finlytics-mau-estimates.xlsx (we added a couple of scenarios based on today's numbers).

Proposed immediate actions:
- Alyssa: confirm expected pilot monthly tokens (min / likely / max) and whether procurement wants a capped spend for pilot.
- We: Karthik will send two concrete pricing options (pilot and production) with explicit $/1M token lines and overage tiers. Lauren will scope suggested soft quota thresholds for your traffic patterns.

If it helps, we can also sketch a short runbook that describes how Redwood handles a 10x burst during market open (routing, temporary throttles, and KV cache behavior).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finlytics call recap — token volumes, target $/1M, and overage approach

Jonas — thanks for the summary and for the materials. Quick answers: 

Pilot sizing (Dec, 30 days):
- Min: 25M tokens
- Expected: 90M tokens
- Max (if we push limits): 200M tokens

Target economics: the $900–1,100 / 1M tokens is our internal target for hosted inference during pilot. We have a separate procurement cap for the pilot at $12k (so we'd be on the lower side of that target).

Rate limits & bursts: market open spikes are the main concern. We need something that won't drop user-facing calls for >5s. Our preferred behavior is:
- Allow short bursts up to 3x baseline for <30s windows (softly enforced)
- Alert + auto-routing to a lower-cost model variant if sustained beyond that window

Procurement is looped on the email — they'll need the exact pilot price line items for approval.

Alyssa
Alyssa Cheng
Head of Product, Finlytics
alyssa@finlytics.com

Disposition: procurement@finlytics.com asked for invoice-ready line items in next email

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@finlytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finlytics call recap — pricing options & overage mechanics (pilot + production)

Alyssa / team — following up with two clean options for the pilot and notes on overage and burst behavior. See bullets below; I'll attach a short table in the HubSpot record for procurement.

Option A — Pilot (monthly, up to 150M tokens)
- Unit price: $975 / 1M tokens (applies to gen + embed tokens)
- Pilot cap: $12,000 (we'll enforce a hard cap unless you opt into auto-overage)
- Burst policy: soft buffer of 2.5x baseline for up to 20s/windows. If burst exceeds buffer, requests are queued for up to 5s, then fail with 429s. We emit alerts and an automated fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical paths.

Option B — Production (monthly commit)
- Committed tier: 1.25B tokens/month at $835 / 1M tokens (volume discount)
- Overage: $1,050 / 1M tokens for consumption beyond committed amount, billed monthly.
- Burst policy: reserved capacity option supports sustained spikes up to 4x baseline for short windows; otherwise same soft buffer & routing.

Prepaid Burst Credits (add-on)
- Pack sizes: 100M / 500M / 1B token packs at 10% discount to listed unit rates; usable during sustained spikes to avoid overage billing.

Notes on behavior and safety valves:
- Soft quota with notifications for pilot by default; can be made hard cap for procurement.
- We can add a 5-minute grace window for the pilot that accumulates short bursts before counting against quota (useful for market open micro-spikes).
- SLA/reserved capacity is available if Finlytics needs zero 429s during spikes — pricing shifts to reserved monthly commits + baseline throughput guarantees.

Next step: Jonas — can you produce the invoice-style PDF for Option A (pilot) that procurement can sign off on? Alyssa — if Option A looks good, confirm whether you want hard cap or auto-overage enabled.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
